Subject: Baseline throughput until full migration complete

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — the infra looked great. We are ramping traffic while our side finishes a week-long model migration. Before we flip the switch on full production, procurement wants a short-term guarantee to avoid outages during the migration window.

Specifically: can Redwood provide a temporary throughput floor (tokens/sec) for our dedicated GPU pool for 72 hours after migration cutover? We understand the long-term SLA will follow the usual reserved-GPU commitments, but procurement needs something in writing that prevents queueing-induced tail latency spikes during the first 3 days.

Appreciate a quick confirmation and any suggestions for clear, testable language.

Cheers,
Maria

Subject: Re: Baseline throughput until full migration complete

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear ask. We can do a short-term, written "SLA bridge" that provides a measurable throughput floor for the 72-hour migration window. High-level proposal:

- Commitment: reserve a minimum of 600 tokens/sec sustained per reserved GPU (equivalent to the burst-adjusted throughput we validated in sandbox) for 72 hours post-cutover.
- Queueing behavior: during the window we will prioritize Acme's requests on the dedicated pool and disable low-priority background batching that can introduce tail latency.
- Remedies: if sustained end-to-end tail latency (95th percentile) exceeds 900ms for more than two 10-minute windows, we will provide a credit equal to 5% of that week’s Dedicated invoice (pro-rated).
- Acceptance test: we will run an agreed test plan (scripted traffic from your load generator + Redwood's telemetry) at T+24 and T+48 to confirm headroom.

I’ve looped in Ben for the technical queueing details and Laura for procurement/legal language and credit mechanics. I’ll also attach a labeled draft SLA for you to share with procurement.

Would you like us to make the draft legally-binding (amendment) or a time-bound commitment note? Either is possible; we usually convert short bridges to an amendment if customers want credits in the contract.

Best,
Soojin

Maria — quick technical clarifications and constraints from the runtime side:

1) The 600 tokens/sec per GPU assumption is based on typical prompt lengths (avg 120 tokens). If your migration uses much longer sequences we should adjust the floor proportionally.

2) "Prioritize" means we will enforce request preemption within the dedicated pool scheduler: Acme requests will be placed into a high-priority lane, and best-effort tenants (if any) will be deprioritized for the 72-hour window. This reduces queuing latency but does not eliminate GPU time-sharing overhead for extremely bursty patterns; we recommend smoothing traffic with short client-side backoff when possible.

3) For the acceptance tests we suggest the following telemetry collection: 95th/99th percentile latency, queue-depth histograms, GPU utilization (%) sampled at 10s intervals, and KV-cache hit-rate. If you can send the attached throughput-logs-0707.csv it will help calibrate the floor.

I'll be available during cutover and can run live traces.

—Ben
